title: Robot
description: A mechanism: a tree of rigid links connected by joints, driven by actuators. Structurally URDF rather than a Denavit-Hartenberg table, because DH has two incompatible conventions in common use and four columns do not record which one they are (ADR-0005). Note what is absent: there is no reach field (ADR-0003) and no payload field (ADR-0004). Both are derived, per-pose, and carry the assumptions that make them true.

make.description: Manufacturer, for a commercial mechanism. Absent for an original design.

kind.description: Open serial chains only. Delta arms, four-bar linkages and differentials are closed chains that the tree in ADR-0005 cannot express, so they are absent rather than approximated.

base_link.description: link_id of the root. The frame every transform in this record is ultimately relative to. Assumed fixed to the world; a mobile base is out of scope (ROADMAP, Not yet).

joints.description: May be empty only for a single-link record. Each joint names a parent and child link_id; the graph must be a tree rooted at base_link, which a validator checks — the schema cannot.

tool.description: The end effector and, more importantly, its offset. A reachability answer is meaningless without the tool offset it assumed, so the verdict carries it (ADR-0003). Null means no tool, which is a declaration, not an omission.

attached_to.description: link_id of the flange this tool bolts to. Defaults to the leaf link.

mass_g.description: A tool's own mass consumes payload capacity before any workpiece does.

measured_payload.description: Only ever figures somebody measured, each naming the pose it was measured at. There is deliberately no scalar payload field: rated capacity falls with extension because load torque is force times moment arm, so one number is true at one configuration and silently wrong everywhere else (ADR-0004). Absent means capacity is derived from continuous actuator torque, or not answered at all.

pose_rad.description: joint_id -> joint value at which the measurement was taken. Radians for revolute joints, millimetres for prismatic ones (the field name follows the dominant case; a validator checks per joint type).

how_measured.description: What was lifted, held for how long, judged by what. A figure with no method behind it is indistinguishable from a recalled one.

sustained.description: Whether the load was held long enough for the actuators to reach thermal steady state. A mass lifted once is not a mass the mechanism can hold.

note.description: Prose. A vendor's published reach figure belongs here if it is worth recording at all — as prose a human reads, never as a field a consumer could mistake for a derived answer (ADR-0003).

link.description: A rigid body. Exactly one of part_id, make or provenance_ref, mirroring OpenBuildCore's three requirement kinds so the vocabularies do not diverge (ADR-0006).

part_id.description: A part from OpenPartsCore. Stored, not resolved: a consumer needing its mass reads the registry. ClawBot imports nothing (ADR-0006).

make.description: Something fabricated rather than bought. Fields match OpenBuildCore's make requirement (its ADR-0006) so a robot's bill of made parts can be handed to its machine check without translation. This is declared design intent, not a measurement.

material.description: Lowercase token, e.g. pla, petg, asa, alu-6061. Required: a made part with no material cannot be checked against a machine at all, and defaulting would invent a design decision on the author's behalf.

provenance_ref.description: An OpenDesignCore artifact. The strongest of the three kinds: the geometry exists, so bbox and volume are facts rather than intent. Same distinction OBC drew between a project's declared size and can-print --from-sidecar.

schema.description: e.g. odc/provenance/0.2 — recorded so a record too old to carry bbox_mm is refused with its schema named rather than silently falling back.

mass_g.description: Only for a link whose mass is not obtainable from its part_id or provenance record. Needed for a static payload derivation; absent means that derivation reports incomplete rather than assuming zero.

type.description: URDF's vocabulary. revolute has limits; continuous rotates without them; prismatic slides; fixed is a rigid attachment that exists to carry a transform.

axis.description: Axis of rotation or translation in the child frame. Required for every type but fixed; a validator enforces that, and also that it is not the zero vector.

limits.description: Absent or null means UNKNOWN, never unlimited. A reachability computation over a joint with no limits answers 'incomplete' and names this joint (ADR-0003), because assuming full travel claims points the mechanism cannot reach.

lower_rad.description: Revolute joints. Bounded at +/- 4*pi deliberately: radians are hostile to hand-authoring and a typed 90 in a _rad field is a plausible mistake, so the range check is the main defence ADR-0005 leaves standing.

effort_nm.description: Maximum torque the joint may be commanded to produce. Distinct from the actuator's continuous torque: this is a limit imposed on the mechanism, that one is what the motor can sustain. A capacity derivation takes the lesser.

actuator_id.description: The actuator driving this joint, from data/actuators/. Absent for a fixed joint, and for a joint moved by hand.

gear_ratio.description: Reduction between actuator output and joint motion, as a multiplier on torque. Efficiency is NOT modelled, so a derived capacity using this is an upper bound and must be labelled one (ADR-0004).

transform.description: A pose relative to the parent frame. Translation in millimetres, rotation as roll/pitch/yaw in radians (ADR-0005). Both default to zero when absent, which is the one safe default here: an omitted transform means the frames coincide, which is a statement, not a guess.

source.description: Where the claim came from. Required on the robot and on every joint, because a joint limit is a physical claim about hardware and the platform gates those on citations. TODO(source) is an acceptable citation string and is expected to fail loudly downstream until replaced — that is what a placeholder is for.
